summary:
Turn 65 confirmed the C1 findings on the amended claim and recorded why the last open issue cannot be resolved by any mechanism the framework accepts.

Resolved substantively. The fresh execution bound to claim version 2 (artifact a0f10ee024ac4ba38d3b84b21a8b40f3, run 32aff0d098454dc78bec6a3916753fa9) reproduced the three in-scope C1 observations — the resolution does not adopt a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED, the recoverer and the committed peer differ, and the disagreement survives the Commit broadcast — and last turn's current-version review accepted their correspondence. The C1 conclusion is therefore confirmed_in_scope again, with the pre-amendment artifacts superseded for basis rather than relied on.

The remaining issue is structurally stuck, and the note records each refusal so no further turn repeats them: resolving it on its own artifact needs a new artifact with the challenged component changed plus a matching fresh execution (its bytes cannot change without an oracle or observation challenge); resolving it on the fresh artifact fails because that artifact is not in the issue's lineage; an ordinary repair must preserve the oracle, which dropping the applied-state property does not; and an encoding revision needs an oracle or observation challenge rather than the scope challenge this issue carries. The boundary it describes is already stated in the amended claim, in claim C3 and in the reviews, so nothing in the findings depends on it.

Final inventory. Ten claims are settled: eight confirmed violations or consequences (C1 recovery divergence, C2 durable-record layout, C3 applied-state divergence, C4 NOOP-commit crash, C6 the promoted-leader variant of C1, C7 the dead accept-rejection path, C9 the recorder's wrong-row write in two scenarios, C10 the command-value truncation with its stream-shift consequence) and two bounded no-violation protections (C5 owner-alive re-proposal, C8 the executor timeout enqueue). Two candidates remain paused with resume conditions (accept-status semantics, client retry). Unread items are named rather than assumed: the reader-side effect of a displaced stream, whether the client caps the command size it builds, and whether any caller enables durable recording. The operational lesson is recorded too: a claim-scope amendment invalidates its artifacts' bases and can strand an issue on a superseded artifact, so such an artifact should be revised in the same cycle as the challenge or the issue accepted as permanently visible. No requirement, premise or observation was weakened.
